items.t: — A new Section 301 regime sets 10% duties on jewelry from India, Canada and the UK and 12.5% on China, Thailand, Turkey and the UAE, live July 24; EU-polished diamonds keep their exemption, goods in transit are spared
— India, which polishes ~90% of the world's diamonds by piece, faces a 10% US duty on polished goods as rough prices sit a third lower YoY; the EU carve-out quietly steers volume toward Antwerp
— Gold ended the week near $4,061/oz, +2% on the week but short of $4,100, as traders positioned for a Fed widely expected to hold on July 29; jobless claims 187k vs 212k forecast
— WPIC forecasts a 297koz platinum deficit for 2026, a fourth straight shortfall, even as spot fell ~1% to $1,574; jewelry demand −12%, bar & coin +27% to 718koz
— Domestic gold fell ~10% in June to a six-month low near ₹141k/10g; listed jewellers logged 30–60% revenue growth, though old-gold trade-ins funded 43–55% of counter sales (WGC)
— Swiss brands raised US list prices ~7% for 2026 while the secondary market slid ~8% to two-year lows for Rolex and Patek, compressing the grey-market premium toward zero
— The São Paulo marquetry house turned straw inlay, Shibayama, abalone and beetle-wing on 1920s geometry — a couture-level Art Deco collection arguing craft, not carat, is the luxury
— Anglo American says De Beers' underlying EBITDA will be negative in H1; consolidated rough revenue −23% to $1.31bn as the sale process to a reported Gareth Penny consortium continues
— Friday's tape divided the precious complex: silver +1.2% to $58.22 while platinum −1.1% to $1,574 and palladium eased to ~$1,225, leaving platinum above palladium into a quiet weekend
